questions.question: A company needs to search for text in documents that are stored in Amazon S3. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: Amazon Kendra is a fully managed intelligent search service designed to index and search unstructured content stored in repositories such as Amazon S3.
keyPoints: Purpose-built for enterprise search over unstructured data
Natively integrates with Amazon S3 as a data source
Uses machine learning and natural language processing
Supports relevance tuning and semantic search
Designed to search text inside documents, not metadata only
Handles formats like PDF, Word, PowerPoint, and text files
examples: Searching policy documents stored as PDFs in an S3 bucket
Allowing employees to query internal documentation using natural language
Indexing knowledge base articles stored in S3 for quick retrieval
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Kendra is specifically designed for searching unstructured enterprise content. Unlike traditional keyword search engines, Kendra understands natural language queries and context, making it ideal for searching document repositories. It directly connects to Amazon S3 buckets, indexes document contents, and applies machine learning models to return the most relevant answers. This makes it the correct choice when the requirement is to search text inside documents rather than perform analytics, image recognition, or text-to-speech operations.

explanation.summary: Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and videos, not text documents.
explanation.why: Rekognition is used for facial recognition, object detection, text-in-image detection, and video analysis. It cannot index or search text-based documents stored in Amazon S3.

explanation.summary: Amazon Polly converts text into lifelike speech.
explanation.why: Polly is a text-to-speech service and does not provide any document indexing or search capabilities.

explanation.summary: Amazon Lex is used to build conversational chatbots and voice assistants.
explanation.why: Lex focuses on natural language interfaces and conversation flows, not searching document repositories.

questions.question: A company needs a fully managed file server that natively supports Microsoft workloads and file systems. The file server must also support the SMB protocol. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: Amazon EFS is a Linux-based file system that uses the NFS protocol.
explanation.why: EFS does not support Windows-native file systems or the SMB protocol required for Microsoft workloads.

explanation.summary: Amazon FSx for Lustre is optimized for high-performance computing workloads.
explanation.why: FSx for Lustre integrates with S3 and supports the Lustre file system, not Windows workloads or SMB.

options.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

explanation.summary: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides a fully managed Windows-native file system with SMB support.
keyPoints: Native support for Windows file systems
Supports features like NTFS, DFS, and file-level permissions
examples: Migrating Windows file shares from on-premises to AWS
Hosting shared drives for Microsoft-based workloads
Supporting Windows applications that require SMB access
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is purpose-built for Microsoft workloads. It provides native SMB support, integrates with Active Directory, and supports Windows-specific features such as NTFS permissions and Distributed File System (DFS). This makes it the correct service when organizations need a managed Windows file server without managing underlying infrastructure.

explanation.summary: Amazon EBS provides block storage for EC2 instances.
explanation.why: EBS is not a file server and does not provide SMB access or managed file sharing.

questions.question: A company wants to move its on-premises databases to managed cloud database services by using a simplified migration process. Which AWS service or tool can help the company meet this requirement?

explanation.summary: AWS Storage Gateway is used for hybrid storage integration.
explanation.why: Storage Gateway focuses on file, volume, and tape storage integration, not database migration.

explanation.summary: AWS Application Migration Service is designed to lift and shift servers.
explanation.why: It migrates entire applications and servers, not database engines into managed database services.

explanation.summary: AWS DataSync is used for transferring large amounts of data.
explanation.why: DataSync moves files and objects, not database schemas or ongoing database replication.

explanation.summary: AWS DMS helps migrate on-premises databases to managed AWS database services with minimal downtime.
keyPoints: Works with managed databases like Amazon RDS and Aurora
examples: Migrating Oracle databases to Amazon RDS
Moving MySQL from on-premises to Amazon Aurora
Keeping source and target databases in sync during migration
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Database Migration Service is specifically built to simplify database migrations. It supports both one-time and continuous replication, allowing organizations to migrate databases with minimal disruption. DMS works with many commercial and open-source databases and integrates seamlessly with managed AWS database services, making it the correct choice for simplified database migration scenarios.

questions.question: A company wants to transform its workforce by attracting and developing a digitally fluent high-performance workforce. The company wants to attract a diverse and inclusive workforce with appropriate mix of technical and non-technical skills. Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) perspective will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: The Business perspective focuses on business outcomes, value realization, and financial management.
explanation.why: The Business perspective addresses strategy, investment, and value, not workforce skills, culture, or talent development.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Caf Business Perspective Aws

explanation.summary: The People perspective focuses on workforce transformation, culture, skills, and organizational change.
keyPoints: Centers on skills, roles, and organizational structure
examples: Upskilling employees with cloud training and certifications
Building cross-functional teams combining business and technical skills
Attracting diverse talent to support innovation and agility
explanation.additionalInfo: The People perspective of the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework addresses how organizations prepare their workforce for cloud adoption. This includes defining new roles, building cloud skills, driving cultural change, and ensuring the organization has the right mix of technical and business capabilities. It explicitly covers diversity, inclusion, training, and change management, making it the correct perspective when the goal is workforce transformation rather than technology or operations.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Caf People Perspective Aws

explanation.summary: The Platform perspective focuses on building and managing cloud infrastructure and platforms.
explanation.why: Platform addresses architecture, networking, and infrastructure services, not workforce development or organizational skills.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Caf Platform Perspective Aws

explanation.summary: The Operations perspective focuses on running and operating workloads.
explanation.why: Operations deals with monitoring, incident response, and operational excellence, not talent strategy or workforce transformation.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Caf Operations Perspective Aws

questions.question: A company wants to provide access to Windows file shares in AWS from its on-premises workloads. The company does not want to provision any additional infrastructure or applications in its data center. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: Amazon FSx File Gateway provides on-premises access to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server without deploying new infrastructure.
keyPoints: Provides SMB access to Windows file shares
Acts as a gateway between on-premises systems and AWS
No need to deploy Windows file servers on premises
Integrates with Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
examples: Accessing AWS-hosted Windows file shares from on-premises applications
Migrating file storage to AWS while keeping existing workflows
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon FSx File Gateway enables hybrid access to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. It allows on-premises applications to use SMB file shares hosted in AWS without deploying or managing additional file servers in the data center. The gateway handles caching and connectivity, making it ideal for extending Windows file shares into AWS with minimal operational change.

explanation.summary: AWS DataSync is used for one-time or recurring data transfers.
explanation.why: DataSync moves data but does not provide ongoing access to Windows file shares.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is object storage, not a Windows file system.
explanation.why: S3 does not provide native SMB access for Windows file shares.

explanation.summary: AWS Snow Family is used for offline data transfer and edge computing.
explanation.why: Snow devices are not designed for continuous access to Windows file shares.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fully managed graph database service on AWS?

explanation.summary: Amazon Aurora is a relational database service.
explanation.why: Aurora supports SQL workloads, not graph data models.

explanation.summary: Amazon FSx is a managed file system service.
explanation.why: FSx provides file storage, not database or graph capabilities.

explanation.summary: Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value and document database.
explanation.why: DynamoDB does not support native graph data models or graph queries.

explanation.summary: Amazon Neptune is a fully managed graph database service.
keyPoints: Designed specifically for graph data models
Supports property graph and RDF models
Uses Gremlin and SPARQL query languages
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Neptune is purpose-built for graph workloads that require traversing complex relationships efficiently. It supports popular graph query languages and is fully managed, handling backups, patching, scaling, and replication. Neptune is the correct choice when applications rely on relationship-heavy data rather than tabular or key-value access patterns.

questions.question: Which AWS Cloud deployment model uses AWS Outposts as part of the application deployment infrastructure?

explanation.summary: On-premises deployments run entirely within a company’s own data center.
explanation.why: AWS Outposts extends AWS infrastructure into on-premises environments but still remains part of AWS, which means the deployment is not purely on-premises.

explanation.summary: Serverless removes infrastructure management from the customer.
explanation.why: Outposts provides physical infrastructure managed by AWS, which does not align with the serverless execution model.

explanation.summary: Cloud-native deployments run fully in AWS Regions.
explanation.why: Outposts places AWS-managed hardware on premises, which goes beyond a purely cloud-native deployment.

explanation.summary: The hybrid deployment model combines on-premises infrastructure with AWS Cloud services.
keyPoints: AWS Outposts extends AWS services to on-premises locations
Provides consistent AWS APIs and tooling
examples: Running latency-sensitive applications on Outposts while using AWS Regions for analytics
Maintaining data residency while using AWS-managed services
Modernizing on-premises workloads with AWS infrastructure
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Outposts is a core component of AWS hybrid cloud strategy. It allows customers to run AWS services on AWS-managed hardware installed in their own data centers. This enables a true hybrid deployment model where applications can span on-premises and AWS Regions using the same APIs, tools, and management practices. Exam questions often associate Outposts directly with hybrid cloud deployments.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate unstructured data to AWS. The data needs to be securely moved with inflight encryption and end-to-end data validation. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: AWS Application Migration Service is used to migrate servers and applications.
explanation.why: It does not focus on large-scale unstructured data transfer with validation and encryption.

explanation.summary: Amazon EFS is a managed file system.
explanation.why: EFS stores data but does not provide migration capabilities with end-to-end validation.

explanation.summary: AWS DataSync securely transfers large amounts of unstructured data with encryption and validation.
keyPoints: Integrates with on-premises storage and AWS services
examples: Migrating file servers to Amazon S3
Moving NAS data to Amazon EFS
Transferring backup archives securely to AWS
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS DataSync is purpose-built for migrating and synchronizing large volumes of unstructured data between on-premises storage systems and AWS storage services. It encrypts data in transit and validates data integrity end to end, ensuring secure and accurate transfers. This makes it the correct choice when security and validation are explicit requirements in a data migration scenario.

explanation.summary: AWS Migration Hub tracks migration progress.
explanation.why: Migration Hub provides visibility and orchestration but does not move data itself.

questions.question: A company’s application developers need to quickly provision and manage AWS services by using scripts. Which AWS offering should the developers use to meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: AWS CLI allows developers to provision and manage AWS services using scripts and commands.
keyPoints: Uses the same APIs as the AWS Management Console
examples: Integrating AWS operations into deployment pipelines
explanation.additionalInfo: The AWS Command Line Interface provides a unified tool to interact with AWS services programmatically. Developers can write scripts to automate provisioning, configuration, and management tasks. Because the CLI directly invokes AWS APIs, it offers the same capabilities as the console while enabling speed, consistency, and automation. This makes it the correct choice for script-driven AWS management.

explanation.summary: AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed build service.
explanation.why: CodeBuild compiles and tests code but does not directly provision or manage AWS services.

explanation.summary: AWS CAF provides guidance and best practices.
explanation.why: CAF is a strategic framework, not a tool for scripting or automation.

explanation.summary: Session Manager provides secure shell access to instances.
explanation.why: It is used for instance access and management, not for provisioning AWS services via scripts.

questions.question: Which Amazon S3 storage class is MOST cost-effective for unknown access patterns?

explanation.summary: S3 Standard is designed for frequent access patterns.
explanation.why: It does not optimize costs when access frequency is unknown or changes over time.

explanation.summary: S3 Standard-IA is designed for known infrequent access patterns.
explanation.why: Using it with unpredictable access can lead to higher retrieval costs.

options.text: S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA)

explanation.summary: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone.
explanation.why: It trades durability for cost savings and still assumes known infrequent access.

explanation.summary: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically optimizes costs for data with unknown or changing access patterns.
keyPoints: Automatically moves objects between access tiers
examples: Data lakes with unpredictable query patterns
explanation.additionalInfo: S3 Intelligent-Tiering is specifically designed for scenarios where access patterns are unknown or change over time. It monitors object access and automatically moves data between frequent and infrequent access tiers without performance impact or retrieval charges. This eliminates the need to predict access patterns upfront and helps minimize storage costs while maintaining durability and availability.

questions.question: A company plans to run a compute-intensive workload that uses graphics processing units (GPUs). Which Amazon EC2 instance type should the company use?

explanation.summary: Accelerated computing instances provide access to GPUs and other hardware accelerators.
keyPoints: Supports machine learning and graphics workloads
explanation.additionalInfo: Accelerated computing EC2 instances are purpose-built to leverage hardware accelerators such as GPUs. These instances are optimized for workloads that benefit from parallel processing, including machine learning, high-performance computing, and graphics rendering. Choosing this instance type ensures access to GPU resources required for compute-intensive applications.

explanation.summary: Compute optimized instances focus on CPU performance.
explanation.why: They do not provide GPUs required for graphics or accelerated workloads.

explanation.summary: Storage optimized instances are designed for high I/O throughput.
explanation.why: They focus on storage performance rather than GPU acceleration.

explanation.summary: General purpose instances balance compute, memory, and networking.
explanation.why: They are not designed to support GPU-based compute workloads.

questions.question: A company wants to verify if multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled for all users within its AWS accounts. Which AWS service or resource will meet this requirement?

explanation.summary: AWS Cost and Usage Report provides billing and usage data.
explanation.why: It does not report on IAM security configurations such as MFA status.

explanation.summary: IAM credential reports provide details about user credentials, including MFA status.
keyPoints: Lists all IAM users in the account
Shows MFA enabled or disabled status
Includes password and access key details
examples: Auditing MFA compliance for IAM users
explanation.additionalInfo: IAM credential reports provide a comprehensive snapshot of IAM user security posture, including whether MFA is enabled. These reports are commonly used during security audits and compliance checks to ensure that all users meet organizational security requirements. They are generated at the account level and can be downloaded as a CSV file for further analysis.

explanation.summary: AWS Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements.
explanation.why: It does not provide visibility into IAM user MFA configuration.

explanation.summary: CloudFront reports focus on content delivery metrics.
explanation.why: They do not include IAM authentication or MFA information.

questions.question: A company wants to use Amazon EC2 instances to provide a static website to users all over the world. The company needs to minimize latency for the users. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use EC2 instances in multiple edge locations.

explanation.summary: Edge locations are used by CloudFront, not for directly running EC2 instances.
explanation.why: EC2 instances cannot be deployed in edge locations. Edge locations are designed for content delivery services, not compute.

options.text: Use EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone but in different AWS Regions.

explanation.summary: Placing instances in the same AZ does not reduce global latency.
explanation.why: Latency reduction requires caching content closer to users, not duplicating instances across Regions without a CDN.

options.text: Use Amazon CloudFront with the EC2 instances configured as the source.

explanation.summary: Amazon CloudFront delivers content globally with low latency by caching it at edge locations.
keyPoints: Caches static content at edge locations
Reduces latency for geographically distributed users
Integrates with EC2 as an origin
examples: Serving static website assets from EC2 via CloudFront
Reducing page load times for global users
Protecting the origin with CloudFront caching
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon CloudFront is the correct solution when minimizing latency for global users. By placing cached copies of static content at edge locations worldwide, CloudFront ensures users are served content from the nearest location. EC2 instances act as the origin, while CloudFront handles distribution, caching, and performance optimization.

options.text: Use EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone but in different AWS accounts.

explanation.summary: Using multiple AWS accounts does not affect latency.
explanation.why: Account separation does not provide geographic distribution or caching benefits.

questions.question: Which of the following is a managed AWS service that is used specifically for extract, transform, and load (ETL) data?

explanation.summary: Amazon Athena is a serverless query service.
explanation.why: Athena queries data but does not perform ETL processing.

explanation.summary: AWS Glue is a fully managed ETL service.
examples: Transforming raw S3 data for analytics
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Glue is purpose-built for extract, transform, and load operations. It provides a serverless environment where users can define ETL jobs without managing infrastructure. Glue also maintains a centralized data catalog that integrates with services such as Athena and Redshift, making it a core data integration service on AWS.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is an object storage service.
explanation.why: S3 stores data but does not perform transformation or loading logic.

explanation.summary: AWS Snowball Edge is used for data transfer and edge computing.
explanation.why: Snowball Edge is not designed for ETL workflows.

questions.question: A company wants to set up its workloads to perform their intended functions and recover quickly from failure. Which pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework aligns with these goals?

explanation.summary: Performance efficiency focuses on using resources efficiently.
explanation.why: It does not primarily address failure recovery or resilience.

explanation.summary: Sustainability focuses on environmental impact.
explanation.why: It does not address system recovery or fault tolerance.

explanation.summary: The Reliability pillar focuses on system recovery, fault tolerance, and resilience.
explanation.additionalInfo: The Reliability pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework addresses a workload’s ability to consistently perform its intended function and recover quickly from failures. It includes best practices such as redundancy, fault isolation, monitoring, and disaster recovery. This pillar is directly aligned with resilience and availability goals.

explanation.summary: Security focuses on protecting data and systems.
explanation.why: It does not primarily address workload recovery from failure.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate its applications to the AWS Cloud. The company plans to identify and prioritize any business transformation opportunities and evaluate its AWS Cloud readiness. Which AWS service or tool should the company use to meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: AWS CAF helps organizations assess cloud readiness and identify business transformation opportunities.
keyPoints: Provides structured guidance for cloud adoption
Aligns cloud strategy with business outcomes
Covers people, governance, platform, and operations
explanation.additionalInfo: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework is designed to help organizations understand their current state and define a structured approach to cloud adoption. It focuses on readiness assessment and transformation planning rather than execution. CAF is typically used at the beginning of a migration journey to identify risks, gaps, and opportunities across business and technical dimensions.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Caf Aws Cloud Adoption

explanation.summary: AWS Managed Services provides operational support for AWS environments.
explanation.why: AMS focuses on ongoing operations and management, not readiness assessment or transformation planning.

explanation.summary: The Well-Architected Framework evaluates existing workloads.
explanation.why: It is used to review architectures, not to assess organizational cloud readiness or business transformation opportunities.

explanation.summary: AWS Migration Hub tracks migration progress.
explanation.why: Migration Hub provides visibility into migrations but does not evaluate readiness or transformation opportunities.

questions.question: A company wants to run a simulation for 3 years without interruptions. Which Amazon EC2 instance purchasing option will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

explanation.summary: Spot Instances can be interrupted at any time.
explanation.why: They are not suitable for long-running workloads that require uninterrupted execution.

explanation.summary: Reserved Instances provide long-term cost savings for steady, uninterrupted workloads.
keyPoints: Offer significant cost savings over On-Demand
explanation.additionalInfo: Reserved Instances are the most cost-effective option for workloads that must run continuously without interruption over long periods. By committing to a one- or three-year term, customers receive discounted pricing compared to On-Demand Instances while maintaining reliability and availability. This makes Reserved Instances ideal for predictable, long-running simulations.

explanation.summary: Dedicated Hosts provide physical server isolation.
explanation.why: They are more expensive and primarily used for licensing or compliance needs, not cost efficiency.

explanation.summary: On-Demand Instances have no long-term commitment.
explanation.why: They are more expensive than Reserved Instances for continuous, long-running workloads.

questions.question: A company wants a customized assessment of its current on-premises environment. The company wants to understand its projected running costs in the AWS Cloud. Which AWS service or tool will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: AWS Trusted Advisor provides best practice recommendations.
explanation.why: It does not perform detailed cost modeling based on on-premises environments.

explanation.summary: Amazon Inspector analyzes security vulnerabilities.
explanation.why: It does not assess infrastructure costs or migration economics.

explanation.summary: AWS Control Tower helps set up and govern multi-account environments.
explanation.why: It does not provide cost assessments for on-premises migrations.

explanation.summary: Migration Evaluator provides a data-driven assessment of on-premises environments and projected AWS costs.
explanation.additionalInfo: Migration Evaluator is specifically designed to help organizations understand the financial implications of moving to AWS. It collects data from on-premises environments and produces detailed cost and usage reports, enabling informed decision-making and accurate budgeting prior to migration.

questions.question: A company plans to migrate to the AWS Cloud. The company is gathering information about its on-premises infrastructure and requires information such as the hostname, IP address, and MAC address. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: AWS DataSync is used for data transfer between storage systems.
explanation.why: DataSync moves files and objects but does not discover infrastructure metadata such as hostnames or MAC addresses.

explanation.summary: AWS Application Migration Service migrates servers and applications.
explanation.why: It focuses on lift-and-shift migrations rather than discovery of detailed on-premises infrastructure metadata.

explanation.summary: AWS Application Discovery Service collects detailed information about on-premises infrastructure.
keyPoints: Collects hostnames, IP addresses, and MAC addresses
Provides data to AWS Migration Hub
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Application Discovery Service is designed to help organizations understand their existing on-premises environments before migrating to AWS. It automatically collects system configuration, network details, and dependency information. This data is essential for accurate migration planning and is commonly visualized in AWS Migration Hub.

explanation.summary: AWS DMS migrates databases to AWS.
explanation.why: It does not collect infrastructure discovery data such as MAC addresses or hostnames.

questions.question: Which task is a responsibility of AWS, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?

explanation.summary: Application-level data protection is shared or customer-managed.
explanation.why: Customers are responsible for encrypting and managing their application data in most scenarios.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Shared Responsibility Model Aws

explanation.summary: User authentication is a customer responsibility.
explanation.why: Customers decide how users authenticate to their applications.

explanation.summary: AWS is responsible for securing the physical infrastructure of the cloud.
keyPoints: Includes data centers and networking hardware
Part of security of the cloud
Customers have no access to physical facilities
explanation.additionalInfo: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, AWS is responsible for security of the cloud. This includes the physical facilities, hardware, and networking infrastructure that run AWS services. Customers are responsible for security in the cloud, such as data protection, identity management, and application configuration.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Shared Responsibility Model Aws

explanation.summary: Firewall configuration is a customer responsibility.
explanation.why: Customers configure security groups, NACLs, and other firewall controls.

questions.question: A user needs to quickly deploy a nonrelational database on AWS. The user does not want to manage the underlying hardware or the database software. Which AWS service can be used to accomplish this?

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service.
explanation.why: It is designed for SQL databases, not nonrelational workloads.

explanation.summary: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database service.
keyPoints: Nonrelational key-value and document data model
Fully managed with no infrastructure management
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon DynamoDB allows users to deploy a nonrelational database quickly without managing servers, storage, or database software. AWS handles provisioning, scaling, patching, and replication automatically. This makes DynamoDB the preferred choice for fast, serverless NoSQL deployments.

explanation.summary: Amazon Aurora is a relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL.
explanation.why: It does not provide a nonrelational data model.

explanation.summary: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse service.
explanation.why: It is optimized for analytics, not operational nonrelational workloads.

questions.question: Which AWS service or resource can be used to identify services that have been used by a user within a specified date range?

explanation.summary: S3 ACLs control access permissions for S3 objects.
explanation.why: ACLs do not track or report which AWS services a user has accessed over time.

explanation.summary: ACM manages SSL and TLS certificates.
explanation.why: It does not provide user activity or service usage tracking.

explanation.summary: Network Access Analyzer evaluates network reachability.
explanation.why: It analyzes network paths and access, not historical service usage by users.

learnMore.title: Vpc Network Access Analyzer Network Access

options.text: AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer

explanation.summary: IAM Access Analyzer helps identify how resources are accessed and which principals are using them.
keyPoints: Analyzes access patterns for IAM principals
Helps identify services accessed by users
Supports analysis over defined time periods
examples: Reviewing which services an IAM user accessed
Identifying unused or overly permissive access
explanation.additionalInfo: IAM Access Analyzer provides visibility into how IAM users and roles access AWS services and resources. It helps security teams understand usage patterns and detect unintended access. While CloudTrail records API calls, exam questions often point to Access Analyzer when identifying which services a user has accessed within a time range.

questions.question: A company wants to use application stacks to run a workload in the AWS Cloud. The company wants to use pre-configured instances. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: Amazon Lightsail provides pre-configured instances and application stacks.
keyPoints: Abstracts much of the AWS infrastructure complexity
Ideal for small to medium workloads
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Lightsail is designed for users who want to deploy applications quickly using pre-configured instances. It offers application stacks such as WordPress, LAMP, and Node.js with simplified management and predictable pricing. This makes Lightsail the correct choice when the requirement explicitly mentions application stacks and pre-configured instances.

explanation.summary: Amazon Athena is a serverless query service.
explanation.why: Athena does not provide application stacks or compute instances.

explanation.summary: AWS Outposts extends AWS infrastructure on premises.
explanation.why: Outposts does not provide pre-configured application stacks.

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 provides raw compute instances.
explanation.why: EC2 requires manual configuration and does not include application stacks by default.

questions.question: A company is migrating to the AWS Cloud. The company wants to understand and identify potential security misconfigurations or unexpected behaviors. The company wants to prioritize any protective controls it might need. Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) security perspective capability will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: Identity and access management focuses on authentication and authorization.
explanation.why: It does not specifically focus on detecting misconfigurations or unexpected behavior.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Caf Security Perspective Aws

explanation.summary: Threat detection focuses on identifying security risks, misconfigurations, and abnormal behavior.
keyPoints: Core capability in CAF security perspective
explanation.additionalInfo: Within the AWS CAF Security perspective, threat detection is the capability responsible for identifying security risks, misconfigurations, and unexpected behaviors. It helps organizations understand their risk exposure and prioritize the protective controls needed during and after migration.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Caf Security Perspective Aws

explanation.summary: Platform engineering focuses on building and operating platforms.
explanation.why: It does not focus on identifying security threats or unexpected behaviors.

explanation.summary: Availability and continuity management focuses on resilience.
explanation.why: It addresses uptime and recovery, not threat or misconfiguration detection.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Caf Operations Perspective Aws

questions.question: A user needs a relational database but does not have the resources to manage the hardware, resiliency, and replication. Which AWS service option meets the user’s requirements?

options.text: Run MySQL on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).

explanation.summary: Running MySQL on ECS requires the customer to manage database operations.
explanation.why: The customer would still be responsible for patching, backups, resiliency, and replication.

explanation.summary: Running MySQL on EC2 is a self-managed database approach.
explanation.why: The customer must manage hardware sizing, patching, backups, and high availability.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS provides a fully managed relational database service.
examples: Using Multi-AZ RDS for fault tolerance
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon RDS offloads database administration tasks such as provisioning, backups, replication, and patching to AWS. This makes it ideal for users who need a relational database but do not want to manage the underlying infrastructure or resiliency mechanisms themselves.

explanation.summary: ElastiCache is an in-memory data store.
explanation.why: It is not a relational database and is not designed for relational workloads.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature gives users the ability to capture information about network traffic in a VPC?

explanation.summary: VPC Flow Logs capture IP traffic metadata for network interfaces in a VPC.
keyPoints: Useful for security analysis and troubleshooting
Can be published to CloudWatch or S3
Works at VPC, subnet, or ENI level
explanation.additionalInfo: VPC Flow Logs record metadata about IP traffic flowing through network interfaces in a VPC. They are widely used for security monitoring, troubleshooting, and compliance. Flow Logs do not inspect packet contents but provide enough information to understand traffic patterns and access decisions.

explanation.summary: Amazon Inspector analyzes vulnerabilities.
explanation.why: It does not capture network traffic metadata.

explanation.summary: Route tables define traffic paths.
explanation.why: They do not log or capture traffic information.

explanation.summary: CloudTrail records API activity.
explanation.why: It does not capture network traffic flowing through VPC interfaces.

questions.question: An Amazon EC2 instance previously used for development is inaccessible and no longer appears in the AWS Management Console. Which AWS service should be used to determine what action made this EC2 instance inaccessible?

explanation.summary: CloudWatch Logs store application and system logs.
explanation.why: They do not provide a full audit trail of management actions on EC2 resources.

explanation.summary: Security Hub aggregates security findings.
explanation.why: It does not track who deleted or modified EC2 resources.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of the AWS account root user?

options.text: The root user is the only user that can be configured with multi-factor authentication (MFA).

explanation.summary: MFA can be enabled for IAM users as well as the root user.
explanation.why: IAM users can and should be configured with MFA. MFA is not exclusive to the root user.

options.text: The root user is the only user that can access the AWS Management Console.

explanation.summary: IAM users can access the AWS Management Console.
explanation.why: Console access is not limited to the root user. IAM users can be granted console access.

options.text: The root user is the first sign-in identity that is available when an AWS account is created.

explanation.summary: The root user is automatically created when an AWS account is created.
keyPoints: Created by default with the AWS account
Has full access to all AWS services and resources
Credentials are tied to the account email address
Should be secured and rarely used
Intended for initial setup and account-level tasks
examples: Enabling MFA on the root account
explanation.additionalInfo: The AWS account root user is the original identity created when the AWS account is opened. It has unrestricted access to all resources in the account and is not subject to IAM permission boundaries. Because of its power, AWS strongly recommends securing the root user with MFA and using it only for tasks that explicitly require root access.

options.text: The root user has a password that cannot be changed.

explanation.summary: The root user password can be changed.
explanation.why: AWS allows the root user password to be reset or changed at any time.

questions.question: Which of the following is entirely the responsibility of AWS, according to the AWS shared responsibility model?

explanation.why: Customers are responsible for training their staff and enforcing internal security practices.

explanation.summary: IAM password policies are configured by customers.
explanation.why: Customers decide password complexity and rotation rules.

options.text: Patching of the guest operating system

explanation.why: Customers manage patching for EC2 instances under the shared responsibility model.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Shared Responsibility Model Aws

explanation.summary: AWS is fully responsible for physical and environmental security.
keyPoints: Covers power, cooling, and environmental safeguards
Part of security of the cloud
explanation.additionalInfo: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, AWS is responsible for the physical and environmental security of its data centers. This includes facilities, hardware, power, and climate controls. Customers are responsible for what they run in the cloud, but AWS is solely responsible for the physical infrastructure.

questions.question: Which AWS Cloud benefit gives a company the ability to quickly deploy cloud resources to access compute, storage, and database infrastructures in a matter of minutes?

explanation.summary: Elasticity focuses on scaling resources up or down.
explanation.why: It does not directly describe rapid provisioning speed.

explanation.summary: Cost savings relate to reduced expenses.
explanation.why: They do not describe speed of deployment.

explanation.summary: Agility refers to the ability to rapidly provision and experiment with resources.
explanation.additionalInfo: Agility is a fundamental cloud computing benefit that allows organizations to provision resources in minutes rather than weeks or months. This speed enables faster innovation, quicker response to market changes, and reduced operational friction compared to traditional on-premises infrastructure.

explanation.summary: Reliability focuses on availability and fault tolerance.
explanation.why: It does not specifically describe rapid provisioning of resources.

questions.question: Who is responsible for managing IAM user access and secret keys according to the AWS shared responsibility model?

options.text: IAM access and secret keys are static, so there is no need to rotate them.

explanation.summary: IAM access keys should be rotated regularly.
explanation.why: Leaving keys static increases security risk and violates AWS best practices.

options.text: The customer is responsible for rotating keys.

explanation.summary: Customers manage IAM users and their credentials.
keyPoints: Customers create and manage IAM users
Customers rotate access and secret keys
Part of security in the cloud
AWS provides tools but does not manage keys
examples: Using IAM roles instead of long-term keys
explanation.additionalInfo: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, AWS is responsible for the security of the cloud, while customers are responsible for security in the cloud. This includes managing IAM users, permissions, and credential rotation. AWS provides services such as IAM and Secrets Manager, but the responsibility for using them correctly lies with the customer.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Shared Responsibility Model Aws

options.text: AWS will rotate the keys whenever required.

explanation.summary: AWS does not automatically rotate IAM access keys.
explanation.why: Key rotation is the customer’s responsibility.

options.text: The AWS Support team will rotate keys when requested by the customer.

explanation.summary: AWS Support does not manage customer credentials.
explanation.why: Credential management is entirely handled by the customer.

questions.question: Which of the following are benefits that a company receives when it moves an on-premises production workload to AWS? (Choose two.)

options.text: AWS trains the company’s staff on the use of all the AWS services.

explanation.summary: AWS training is optional and not automatically included.
explanation.why: Training services are separate offerings and not a guaranteed benefit of migration.

options.text: AWS manages all security in the cloud.

explanation.summary: Security responsibilities are shared.
explanation.why: Customers remain responsible for security in the cloud.

options.text: AWS offers free support from technical account managers (TAMs).

explanation.summary: TAMs are part of Enterprise Support.
explanation.why: They are not free and require an Enterprise Support plan.

explanation.summary: AWS infrastructure is designed for high availability.
examples: Using managed services with built-in failover
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS provides a highly available global infrastructure with multiple Regions and Availability Zones. This allows customers to design resilient architectures that can withstand failures and maintain service availability, which is a key benefit of migrating production workloads to AWS.

explanation.summary: AWS achieves cost efficiencies through economies of scale.
examples: Lower storage costs compared to on premises
explanation.additionalInfo: Economies of scale are a fundamental cloud benefit. By operating at massive global scale, AWS can offer lower prices than most organizations could achieve on their own. These savings are passed on to customers, making cloud adoption more cost-effective for production workloads.

questions.question: A company wants to migrate petabytes of data from its on-premises data center to AWS. The company does not want to use an internet connection to perform the migration. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: AWS DataSync transfers data over the network.
explanation.why: It requires network connectivity and is not designed for offline petabyte-scale transfers.

explanation.summary: Amazon Connect is a cloud contact center service.
explanation.why: It has no role in data migration or physical transfer.

explanation.summary: AWS Snowmobile is designed for exabyte- and petabyte-scale data transfers.
keyPoints: Supports petabytes to exabytes of data
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Snowmobile is a truck-mounted data transfer service capable of moving extremely large datasets without using the internet. It is specifically intended for petabyte-scale migrations where network-based transfer would be impractical, slow, or costly.

explanation.summary: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated network connection.
explanation.why: It still relies on network transfer and is not ideal for petabyte-scale one-time migrations.

questions.question: A company has a physical tape library to store data backups. The tape library is running out of space. The company needs to extend the tape library’s capacity to the AWS Cloud. Which AWS service should the company use to meet this requirement?

explanation.summary: Amazon EFS is a managed NFS file system.
explanation.why: EFS does not emulate tape libraries or integrate with tape backup workflows.

explanation.summary: Amazon EBS provides block storage for EC2.
explanation.why: EBS cannot act as a virtual tape library.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is object storage.
explanation.why: S3 alone does not integrate directly with existing tape-based backup software.

explanation.summary: AWS Storage Gateway provides a virtual tape library (VTL) for backup workflows.
keyPoints: Extends on-premises tape libraries to AWS
Stores virtual tapes in Amazon S3
examples: Extending backup capacity without new hardware
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Storage Gateway includes a Tape Gateway configuration that presents a virtual tape library to existing backup software. This allows organizations to extend or replace physical tape libraries while continuing to use familiar backup tools, with data stored durably in Amazon S3 and Glacier.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Shared Responsibility Model Aws

questions.question: A company wants to create a globally accessible ecommerce platform for its customers. The company wants to use a highly available and scalable DNS web service to connect users to the platform. Which AWS service will meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 provides compute resources.
explanation.why: It does not provide DNS services.

explanation.summary: Amazon VPC provides network isolation.
explanation.why: It does not offer DNS routing for internet-facing applications.

explanation.summary: Amazon Route 53 is a highly available and scalable DNS service.
examples: Routing users to global ecommerce platforms
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Route 53 provides global DNS resolution with built-in health checks and routing policies. It is commonly used to connect users to highly available and scalable applications, making it the correct choice for globally accessible ecommerce platforms.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS is a managed database service.
explanation.why: It does not provide DNS-based traffic routing for users.

questions.question: A company is migrating its workloads to the AWS Cloud. The company must retain full control of patch management for the guest operating systems that host its applications. Which AWS service should the company use to meet these requirements?

explanation.summary: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database service.
explanation.why: It does not provide access to or control over guest operating systems.

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 provides full control over the guest operating system.
keyPoints: Full control over patching and updates
Required when OS-level control is needed
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon EC2 operates under the infrastructure as a service (IaaS) model, where AWS manages the underlying hardware and virtualization layer, but customers retain full control over the guest operating system. This makes EC2 the correct choice when organizations must manage patching, updates, and configuration of the OS themselves.

explanation.summary: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service.
explanation.why: It does not provide access to or control over the underlying operating system.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS is a managed database service.
explanation.why: The operating system is managed by AWS, not the customer.

questions.question: A company is planning to host its workloads on AWS. Which AWS service requires the company to update and patch the guest operating system?

explanation.summary: Amazon DynamoDB is fully managed.
explanation.why: AWS handles patching and maintenance.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is a fully managed object storage service.
explanation.why: There is no guest operating system for customers to patch.

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 requires customers to manage the guest operating system.
explanation.additionalInfo: With Amazon EC2, AWS provides the compute infrastructure, but customers are responsible for managing the guest operating system. This includes installing updates, applying security patches, and configuring the OS according to organizational requirements.

learnMore.title: Whitepapers Aws Shared Responsibility Model Aws

questions.question: A company website is experiencing DDoS attacks. Which AWS service can help protect the company website against these attacks?

explanation.summary: AWS Resource Access Manager is used to share resources across accounts.
explanation.why: It does not provide DDoS protection capabilities.

explanation.summary: AWS Amplify is used for application development and hosting.
explanation.why: It is not a DDoS protection service.

explanation.summary: AWS Shield provides protection against distributed denial of service attacks.

Available in Standard and Advanced tiers
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Shield is a managed DDoS protection service that safeguards applications running on AWS. explanation.summary: Amazon GuardDuty detects threats using logs and events.
explanation.why: It detects suspicious activity but does not actively mitigate DDoS attacks.

questions.question: Which AWS service or feature is a browser-based, pre-authenticated service that can be launched directly from the AWS Management Console?

Integrated with the AWS Management Console

questions.question: At what support level do users receive access to a support concierge?

questions.question: A company needs to organize its resources and track AWS costs on a detailed level. The company needs to categorize costs by business department, environment, and application. Which solution will meet these requirements?

Cost allocation tags map costs to business dimensions
Integrate with Cost Explorer and CUR
explanation.additionalInfo: Using resource tags and activating them as cost allocation tags is the standard AWS approach for detailed cost tracking. options.text: Create Amazon CloudWatch dashboards to visually organize and track costs individually.

questions.question: A company wants a unified tool to provide a consistent method to interact with AWS services. Which AWS service or tool will meet this requirement?
